My go-to transcription tool on Mac, MacWhisper, has received another big update today, with real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and a brand-new transcription model. Here's what's new.

MacWhisper deepens Apple Intelligence integration

I've written before about how much I rely on MacWhisper, particularly for incorporating it into my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first tools to offer AI-powered transcription on the Mac. Since its launch in 2023 by independent developer Jordi Bruin, it has continued to improve and expand its support for new models, services, and workflows.

Those improvements have included automatic meeting recording, speaker identification, watched folders, system-wide dictation, local and cloud-based AI models, and integrations with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper is being upgraded to version 15.2, introducing enhanced speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was announced just a few hours ago.

Which brings us to another major new feature in this update: real-time meeting transcription.

This feature has been high on MacWhisper's public roadmap for a while, and now it's finally here, allowing users to view, search back through, copy, or send live transcription text while a meeting is in progress.

In terms of the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, which supports 22 languages, and features tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts in macOS 27.

Now, users on macOS (including those in the European Union) can search transcripts system-wide, open them with Siri, add their text to Shortcuts, and reference the transcript currently on screen in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 introduces folders and subfolders for organising transcripts and meetings, and supports dragging existing transcripts into them from the sidebar.
